subsystems.name: Seed unit
subsystems.role: a micron-scale starter package holding the blueprint, a small power source and the tools to begin growing a structure.
parts: instruction storage (e.g. synthetic DNA or sequence-defined polymer)

subsystems.name: Molecular assemblers
subsystems.role: position individual atoms and molecules precisely so they bond where the blueprint says.
parts: scanning-probe-style or mechanically constrained tool tip

subsystems.name: Feedstock capture
subsystems.role: gathers carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and trace elements from the air and surroundings.
parts: CO2 capture chemistry (amine or solid sorbent)
catalyst to release and reduce carbon

subsystems.name: Structural synthesis
subsystems.role: turns simple molecules into strong building material.

subsystems.name: Error correction
subsystems.role: keeps defects from multiplying as the structure grows.

subsystems.name: Power and heat management
subsystems.role: delivers energy to millions of tiny workers and removes the heat that reactions produce.
parts: thermal gradient management (Brownian motion never stops at this scale)

subsystems.name: Global control
subsystems.role: coordinates the swarm so it builds the intended shape and stops at the end.

buildSteps.title: Design the structure and the growth rules
buildSteps.detail: Engineers specify not just the finished building but the local rules each unit follows, so that simple steps produce the whole shape — the same logic as self-assembling DNA structures, scaled up by many orders of magnitude.

buildSteps.title: Encode the blueprint
buildSteps.detail: Instructions are written into a durable chemical sequence that a seed can read and copy.

buildSteps.title: Make one seed, top-down
buildSteps.detail: Because no self-replicating machine exists yet, the first seed would be fabricated with today's nanolithography and probe-based atom manipulation — slow, expensive, and only at laboratory scale.

buildSteps.title: Capture feedstock
buildSteps.detail: The seed and its copies pull carbon dioxide from air at roughly 420 parts per million and water from the environment, using sorbents and catalysts; this step needs a large continuous energy input.

buildSteps.title: Replicate the seed
buildSteps.detail: Copies build copies, with proofreading to limit the error rate, until enough workers exist to cover a building site. Non-biological replication at useful speed has never been demonstrated.

buildSteps.title: Assemble primary structure
buildSteps.detail: Copies position themselves along designed paths and lay down load-bearing members molecule by molecule, growing from millimetres to metres over months.

buildSteps.title: Consolidate and integrate services
buildSteps.detail: Bulk material is filled in, then channels for air, water, power and data are grown or inserted as the structure rises.

buildSteps.title: Verify and hand over
buildSteps.detail: The finished building is inspected against the blueprint; residual seeds are deactivated with the kill switch and recovered.

prerequisites.why: individual atoms have been placed with scanning probe tips and limited tip-driven bond formation has been shown, but never as a fast, general manufacturing method.
the whole concept depends on machines making copies of themselves cheaply and accurately; no such system exists, and error rates compound catastrophically.
biology proofreads DNA; equivalent machinery for a synthetic builder has not been built.

prerequisites.tech: Direct air capture at low energy cost
prerequisites.why: pilot plants capture carbon dioxide from air today, but they are energy-hungry and produce far less material than a building would need.
molecular dynamics and computational protein design can model small systems, not a whole self-assembling structure.
at this size viscous drag dominates and heat is hard to shed; supplying and controlling energy to billions of units is unsolved.

pathway.milestone: laboratory self-assembly: DNA origami, self-assembled monolayers, and atom-by-atom manipulation with probe microscopes
pathway.unlocks: proof that molecules can be programmed to arrange themselves into designed shapes, at micrometre scale and below.

pathway.milestone: engineered hierarchical self-assembly of useful materials, plus self-assembling and self-healing composites
pathway.unlocks: structures that grow or repair themselves at centimetre scale without human hands.

pathway.milestone: reprogrammable matter at millimetre scale — modular robotic building blocks that reorganise on command
pathway.unlocks: shape-changing construction at building scale, though powered by conventional motors rather than molecular tools.

pathway.milestone: a demonstrably self-replicating, error-corrected molecular manufacturing system in the laboratory
pathway.unlocks: the first credible route from a seed to a grown structure.
construction with far less transport and mining — if the energy, heat and safety problems can ever be solved.
